- [`model-semantics/union-normalization.json`](model-semantics/union-normalization.json): nested open vocabularies, source-aware uniform folds, numeric range widths and native enum/const pin payloads.
- [`model-semantics/root-kind-unions.json`](model-semantics/root-kind-unions.json): independent root native payload wrappers, named null/ref/list/suffix, tagged Unknown versus closed nullable-polymorphic serializers.
- [`model-semantics/root-unions.json`](model-semantics/root-unions.json): standalone-root content versus default polymorphism, enum constructors, root refs/lists/recursive DTOs, escaped implicit refs/suffix wire tags, const singletons and raw Unknown.
- [`model-semantics/object-unions.json`](model-semantics/object-unions.json): nested variants, common defaults, tag/multi-enum/required-key mixed dispatch, const singletons, Unknown raw passthrough, refs/allOf/nested/items/suffix and real serializer contracts.
- [`model-semantics/primitive-unions.json`](model-semantics/primitive-unions.json): inline kind dispatch, sibling wrappers, one object/ref/const shape, arrays, nulls, nested/suffix scopes and real serializer contracts.
- [`model-semantics/enum-contexts.json`](model-semantics/enum-contexts.json): typeless string enums and native numeric/boolean inline/item/nested mappings, membership warnings and real serializer contracts.
- [`model-semantics/object-composition.json`](model-semantics/object-composition.json): multi-level object merges, overrides, reference wrappers and nested/list/suffix serialization contracts.
- [`model-semantics/const-fields.json`](model-semantics/const-fields.json): scalar body defaults, always-encode behavior, nested/list/ref/suffix contracts and generated serialization-constructor boundaries.
- [`model-semantics/nullable-composition.json`](model-semantics/nullable-composition.json): nullable oneOf/anyOf properties, references, nested objects and list-item runtime contracts.
- [`model-semantics/primitive-components.json`](model-semantics/primitive-components.json): component aliases/ref/array/suffix scalar contracts, supplemented by generated JVM-width boundaries.
- [`model-semantics/enum-naming.json`](model-semantics/enum-naming.json): enum constant spellings, reserved/collision suffixes, operators, Unicode, empty values and string lookups.
- [`model-semantics/open-enums.json`](model-semantics/open-enums.json): component/ref/inline/array/suffix enum runtime contracts; this focused input supplements the P1 inventory.
- [`catalog.json`](catalog.json): a compact introductory example and Kotlin compilation smoke input.
- [`p1/`](p1/README.md): 154 historical named inputs (38 original successes, 116 original rejection expectations), and 50 unchanged Kotlin snapshots. Seven scalar cases, one array-component case and the direct empty nullable-component case now have explicit positive graduation contracts; 107 remain rejected.
- [`p1/cases.json`](p1/cases.json): the executable inventory. Every input declares its options and either exact expected files or an error code and JSON Pointer.

## Execution

```bash
# Both core and real CLI run every inventory entry.
GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off go test -count=1 -v ./core ./internal/cli

# Large inputs are built in memory instead of committing multi-megabyte fixtures.
GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off go test -count=1 ./core ./internal/document ./internal/output

# One compiler invocation for real outputs from all positive inputs.
bash scripts/test.sh models --offline
```

The core tests compare entire generated source sets, repeat generation, and reorder component inventories without reordering properties. Negative tests assert exact diagnostic codes and pointers.

CLI tests execute `generate`, `validate` and `generate --check`. Each negative case runs against an existing generated tree plus a handwritten file and must preserve their bytes and mtimes. Positive cases verify fresh-output check differences, exact sources, successful checks, validation, and no-op stability. Suffix validation is tested only by `generate`, since `validate` has no suffix option.

The inventory checker fails on missing files, orphaned inputs/snapshots, duplicate IDs, unknown inventory fields and unsafe paths. The shared loader lives in [`internal/testutil/corpus.go`](../../internal/testutil/corpus.go); expectations are not inferred from current generator output.

## Adding or changing a fixture

1. Add a focused `.json` under `p1/valid` or `p1/invalid` and an entry to `p1/cases.json` with a unique ID and a reason for the case.
2. For successful inputs, independently specify and review **all** expected Kotlin files under `p1/snapshots/<id>/`. Use a distinct package for each positive case so all real generated outputs can compile together.
3. For rejected inputs, specify the stable diagnostic code and exact pointer (`null` for document syntax/options errors). Keep deferred semantics in separate cases so one unsupported keyword cannot mask another.
4. Run core/CLI corpus tests. Run the single Kotlin compilation when a positive case exercises a new output shape. Update this coverage summary when counts change.

Nine syntax-negative `.json` files intentionally contain invalid JSON or duplicate keys. Do not repair or reformat them as ordinary examples. Use the inventory's `E_JSON_INVALID` entries to identify them; all other cases must remain syntactically valid JSON.

Resource tests cover the exact 8 MiB input boundary, invalid UTF-8, schema-depth success/failure boundaries, deep metadata, and JVM constructor-slot limits including primitive width and nullable boxing. Temporary-filesystem transaction tests separately cover manifest corruption, ownership, locks, symlinks and rollback; these are not JSON-schema features.
